tools.name: search_datadog_logs
tools.description: Searches logs with filters (time, query, service, host, storage tier, and so on) and returns log details. Renamed from `get_logs`.

query.description: Log search query in Datadog syntax, for example service:api env:prod status:error.

from.description: Start of the time range: a relative time such as now-1h, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now-1h.

to.description: End of the time range: now, a relative time, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now.

storage_tier.description: Log storage tier to search, for example indexes or flex.

head_limit.description: The most log entries to return. Default 100.

extra_fields.description: Extra fields to return with each log.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: analyze_datadog_logs
tools.description: Analyze Datadog logs using SQL queries for counting, aggregations, and numerical analysis. Use this for statistical analysis.

query.description: SQL query over the logs table, for example SELECT service, count(*) FROM logs GROUP BY service.

filter.description: Log filter in Datadog syntax that limits the rows the SQL query sees, for example service:api.

from.description: Start of the time range: a relative time such as now-1h, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now-1h.

to.description: End of the time range: now, a relative time, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now.

storage_tier.description: Log storage tier to analyze, for example indexes or flex.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: get_datadog_metric
tools.description: Queries and analyzes historical or real-time metric data, supporting custom queries and aggregations.

query.description: Metric query in Datadog syntax, for example avg:system.cpu.user{env:prod} by {host}.

from.description: Start of the time range: a relative time such as now-1h, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now-1h.

to.description: End of the time range: now, a relative time, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now.

raw_data.description: Return raw data points instead of binned values.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: get_datadog_metric_context
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a metric or derived metric, including metadata, available tags, and tag values for filtering and grouping.

metric_name.description: Name of the metric to describe, for example system.cpu.user.

include_tag_values.description: Also list the values of each tag.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: search_datadog_metrics
tools.description: Lists available metrics, with options for filtering and metadata.

name_filter.description: Glob that metric names must match, for example cockroachdb.*.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: search_datadog_monitors
tools.description: Retrieves information about Datadog monitors, including their statuses, thresholds, and alert conditions.

query.description: Monitor search query, for example status:alert or tag:team:payments.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: search_datadog_events
tools.description: Searches events like monitor alerts, deployment notifications, infrastructure changes, security findings, and service status changes.

query.description: Event search query in Datadog syntax, for example source:deployment service:api.

from.description: Start of the time range: a relative time such as now-1h, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now-1h.

to.description: End of the time range: now, a relative time, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: search_datadog_incidents
tools.description: Retrieves a list of Datadog incidents, including their state, severity, and metadata.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: get_datadog_incident
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about an incident.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: search_datadog_spans
tools.description: Retrieves spans from APM traces with filters such as service, time, resource, and so on.

query.description: Span search query in Datadog syntax, for example service:checkout status:error.

from.description: Start of the time range: a relative time such as now-1h, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now-1h.

to.description: End of the time range: now, a relative time, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now.

head_limit.description: The most spans to return. Default 100.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: aggregate_spans
tools.description: Aggregates APM spans to compute counts, sums, averages, minimums, maximums, cardinality, and percentiles (p50 to p99). Group results by fields such as service or resource, or set `group_by.interval` in milliseconds to return a timeseries.

query.description: Span filter in Datadog syntax, for example service:checkout.

from.description: Start of the time range: a relative time such as now-1h, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now-1h.

to.description: End of the time range: now, a relative time, or an ISO 8601 time. Default now.

compute.description: What to compute: an aggregation such as count, avg, sum, min, max, cardinality or a percentile from p50 to p99, with an optional metric.

group_by.description: Group the results by fields such as service or resource. Set interval, in milliseconds, to return a time series.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: get_datadog_trace
tools.description: Fetches a complete trace from Datadog APM using a trace ID.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.

tools.name: search_datadog_entities
tools.description: Searches Datadog's Catalog for service identity, ownership and upstream and downstream dependencies.

query.description: What to find in the Datadog catalog: a service name, an owner, or a dependency question.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens the answer may take. Longer results are cut.
